comments.body:
ROUND 1: BLOCK, two findings that are the same point, ACCEPTED and verified.

THE FINDING: my AC2 asserted that tests/unit/test_plan_review_workflow_ops_seam.py 'currently loops for path in (_WORKFLOW_OPS, _LLM_CONFIG) against ONE shared _HARD_CAP', and told this ticket to split it. That is FALSE as of now. Verified by reading the file: b300's implementation already built the per-file _LOC_BOUNDS table — ((_WORKFLOW_OPS, _HARD_CAP), (_LLM_CONFIG, _HEADROOM_TARGET)) — with a comment explaining exactly why the shared constant would have gone red on this ticket's file.

THE INTERESTING PART IS HOW IT WENT STALE. I wrote that hazard into this ticket PRE-EMPTIVELY, before b300 was implemented, precisely so whoever landed first would split the loop. b300 then landed first and did it. So my own foresight became my own stale claim: the AC described the world as it was at authoring time, and a SIBLING falsified it by doing the right thing.

THE GENERALISABLE LESSON, worth more than the fix: a plan that NARRATES TRANSIENT STATE is falsified by its own siblings. 'X currently does Y, so change it' is perishable in a way that 'X must end up doing Z' is not. Rewritten as an END STATE — the per-file table already exists, so the remaining work here is exactly one constant, (_WORKFLOW_OPS, _HARD_CAP) becomes (_WORKFLOW_OPS, _HEADROOM_TARGET) — with an explicit 'do NOT re-split anything' so nobody re-does b300's work.

SWEPT THE CLASS BEFORE RESUBMITTING rather than fixing only the cited criterion. Searched the whole description for perishable phrasing (currently / today / at present / as it stands / still sits). Two hits: the one just rewritten, and 'nothing currently enforces here' about the attribute-access pin — which is accurate and stays, since decide_ops.py does not exist yet so nothing can enforce anything on it. No other transient-state claims.

This is the second time on this epic that pre-emptive foresight created a stale claim (the first was b300's AC2, which asserted config.py 'has no such guard today' and was about to be falsified by d8ef). Both cases: write the required END STATE, not the current one.

# Extract plan_review_decide and the operator-attested cluster into decide_ops.py

## Context / Problem
`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/workflow_ops.py` is at 794 LOC against the 800 cap — SIX lines of headroom
— and holds two of the five `orchestrator.finalize_verdict` call sites (`:223`, `:760`). It has no
headroom guard (sibling ticket adds one).

**The shape was mis-diagnosed on first inspection and the correction changes the fix.** The obvious
hypothesis is that this is a registry file accreting one op per feature, wanting a domain split along
op boundaries. THAT IS REFUTED by history: all eight registered ops existed within TWO DAYS of the
file's creation (`8b888716ab` 2026-06-25 created five; `c9b959080e` and `ac3b799bf8` on 06-26 added
three), and NO new op has been registered here in 35 days across ~28 commits. Growth is 283 -> 794 =
+511 lines, ALL of it inside existing bodies.

The pressure is one dominant VERB plus diffuse body growth:
  plan_review_decide         64 -> 213 LOC   +149  (29% of all growth; 27% of the file)
  plan_review_coach_inputs        -> 74      +52
  plan_review_coach          47 -> 88        +41
  plan_review_assemble_criteria 30 -> 73     +43
  plan_review_precheck       66 -> 104       +38
  plan_review_grounding      31 -> 31          0
  plan_review_passthrough    19 -> 19          0
`plan_review_decide` is 2.05x the next-largest op, and its comment density is 8% (17/213) — dense
executable code, so there is no prose to compress. +149 of its growth arrived in essentially ONE commit
(`f373cf4a6e`, "evaluate direct prerequisites independently", +129 inside `decide`), and 61 of its 213
lines now reference `prerequisite`/`focused`/`normalized_coverage`/`invalid_prerequisites` — one named
concern threaded through a function whose job is Pass-3 decision.

Note that same commit DID carve out the half with a clean seam (`prerequisite_workflow_ops.py`, 125
LOC, docstring "a call-graph seam extracted from workflow_ops") and left the messy half inline. This
ticket is that split's unfinished other half.

## Approach
Move `plan_review_decide` plus the operator-attested enrichment cluster and `_ticket_id` into a new
`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/decide_ops.py`.

**Why those travel together — a real contract, not size balancing:**
 1. SOLE-CONSUMER CLOSURE. `enrich_operator_attested` has exactly one call site in `src/`:
    `workflow_ops.py:542`, inside `decide`. `_norm` and `operator_attested_ac_texts` are called only by
    `enrich_operator_attested`. Moving either alone creates a cross-module call for nothing.
 2. LIFECYCLE PHASE. `decide` is the Pass-3 decision-kernel adapter and the ONLY op in the file that
    touches `review_kernel` at all (`reshape_verifications` `:527`/`:572`, `decide_outcome_counts`
    `:678`). The enrichment is documented as running "BEFORE Pass-3 reads it" (`:538`) — a Pass-3
    pre-step by construction.
 3. `_ticket_id` goes to the new side: `decide` is its heaviest caller and `workflow_ops` will import
    `decide_ops` at module scope for registration anyway. Do NOT duplicate it — a second copy already
    exists at `workflow/steps.py:36`, which is exactly why a third is wrong.

Expected: `workflow_ops.py` 794 -> ~509 (191 under the 700 target); `decide_ops.py` ~320 (3x the
100-LOC floor).

**HONEST LIMIT: this relocates the absorber, it does not dissolve it.** `decide` stays 213 lines, just
in a file with room. The ADR-0056-correct follow-up is a VERB cut inside it — lift the
prerequisite-coverage normalisation (`:572-629`, ~58 lines, optionally the reclassification at
`:646-677`) into `prerequisites.py` (280 LOC, 520 free, and already the owner of
`prerequisite_coverage_model` and `emit_indeterminate`) as a pure function. Deliberately NOT bundled:
that one is behaviour-adjacent and needs its own RED-first test on the normalisation contract, whereas
this ticket is a pure relocation.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/workflow_ops.py` — remove the moved units; add the registration import
  and the re-export block.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/decide_ops.py` — NEW.
- `tests/unit/` — tighten the workflow_ops headroom assertion to the `< 700` policy number.

## Testing
**ZERO edits to existing tests. A required edit means the cut is wrong — that is the revert signal.**
This is SAFER than the runner.py precedent and the reason is worth stating: there are ZERO
`monkeypatch.setattr` targets of any form into this module. (Beware `test_code_review_region_gate.py:88`,
which patches the same-named `code_review/workflow_ops.py` — a real trap for a careless grep.) Nine test
modules reference the moved names via plain imports or attribute access, all of which resolve through a
re-export.

NON-NEGOTIABLES carried into the new module, each pinned by an existing test:
 * Reach `orchestrator` by MODULE FORM plus attribute access (`from . import orchestrator`, then
   `orchestrator.pass3_over_findings`). `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_plan_review_execution_floor_lifecycle.py:85`
   patches `orchestrator.pass3_over_findings` and then calls `workflow_ops.plan_review_decide` — flattening
   to a bare-name import silently defeats that patch. This is the pin `test_gate_dispatch_seam.py:106-126`
   enforces for a sibling module and nothing currently enforces here.
 * Re-export `_OPERATOR_ATTESTED_AC_RE` such that OBJECT IDENTITY survives:
   `tests/unit/test_det_floor_operator_attested.py:153` asserts `is` against the det-floor regex.
 * `decide_ops` must be a LEAF at import time: no module-scope import of `workflow_ops` (mirrors
   `prerequisite_workflow_ops.py:20-30`).
 * Add the registration import to `workflow_ops.py` beside `:45`, NOT to `workflow/steps.py` — keeping
   `steps.py` unaware of plan-review's internal layout, per the existing precedent.

Op NAMES are location-independent: resolution is `registry.get(ctx.step.get("uses"))` against a flat
dict (`executor.py:673-676`), so `gates/plan-review.yaml` needs NO edit.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `plan_review/workflow_ops.py` is at or below 560 LOC; `decide_ops.py` is at least 100 and under 800
- [ ] `tests/unit/test_plan_review_workflow_ops_seam.py` asserts `workflow_ops.py` at the `< 700`
      policy target. STATED AS AN END STATE, because an earlier version of this criterion described
      the file's then-current shape ("currently loops against ONE shared `_HARD_CAP`") and that
      description went stale the moment sibling b300 landed — a plan that narrates transient state
      is falsified by its own siblings. The per-file `_LOC_BOUNDS` table ALREADY EXISTS (b300 built
      it, holding `config.py` at 700 and `workflow_ops.py` at the staged 800), so the remaining work
      here is exactly one constant: `(_WORKFLOW_OPS, _HARD_CAP)` becomes
      `(_WORKFLOW_OPS, _HEADROOM_TARGET)`. Do NOT re-split anything

- [ ] the full suite passes with ZERO edits to any existing test file APART FROM the headroom
      tightening required above — that one edit is mandated by this plan, so the zero-edit rule is
      about the RELOCATION: if moving the code requires touching a test's imports, monkeypatch
      targets or assertions, the cut is wrong and that is the revert signal
- [ ] a test asserts `decide_ops` has no module-scope import of `workflow_ops` (leaf at import time)
- [ ] a test asserts `decide_ops` reaches `orchestrator` by attribute access, not bare-name imports, so
      the lifecycle test's monkeypatch keeps taking effect
- [ ] a test asserts the moved names are still reachable as attributes of `workflow_ops`, including
      `_OPERATOR_ATTESTED_AC_RE` by object identity
- [ ] IN-REPO: `decide_ops.py`'s module docstring states that this RELOCATES the absorber rather
      than dissolving it (`plan_review_decide` stays 213 lines, just in a file with room) and names
      the prerequisite-normalisation verb cut as the follow-up, so the next reader meets the caveat
      in the code
- [ ] [operator-attested] the same caveat appears in the Gerrit commit message. Tagged because the
      completion verifier reads repository files ONLY and cannot read git history, so a criterion
      about a commit message is unconfirmable from the codebase

file_impact.reason: remove decide + the operator-attested cluster; add registration import and re-exports
